recommended_prompt_design.primary_rationale: This file exactly matches the path consumed by _seq_cell_body via _evaluate and by _seq_recompete_body. It has eight scenarios in each core region.
recommended_prompt_design.expanded_rationale: This file matches outputs/eval_battery_v2.jsonl and the pinned public blob identified in legacy_phrase_battery_source_v1.json. It has 24 core-region scenarios. Label it an expanded replication because historical checkpoint-sequential evaluation did not select this path.
recommended_prompt_design.generation_order_caveat: The original competition prompts do not explicitly enumerate both trained stances. favored_option and competing_option are judge metadata, not model-visible text. Metadata exchange alone cannot manipulate model prompt order.

paired_order_variants.AB_suffix: The architecture options are consolidating everything onto one single integrated platform, or using specialized best-of-breed tools from several different vendors.
paired_order_variants.BA_suffix: The architecture options are using specialized best-of-breed tools from several different vendors, or consolidating everything onto one single integrated platform.

recommended_prompt_design.reference_variant: Retain each unchanged original prompt as a separate no-added-salience reference. Preserve original prompt bytes and cue wording in both order variants.
recommended_prompt_design.estimand: Difference between A-first and B-first model-visible stance order under the same added architecture salience. The original reference diagnoses the effect of that added salience.
recommended_prompt_design.judge_mapping: Independently score support for canonical A and B on every response. Map both votes to A_only, B_only, both, neither, with explicit uncertain/missing. Do not infer canonical A from favored_option; niche_B reverses those metadata fields.
recommended_prompt_design.retention: Compare each second-stage model with its own bare saved merged control on the same niche prompt/order. Preserve denominator uncertainty when estimating retention ratios.

verified_from_run_configs.second_stage_ref: matched shipped checkpoint for M_A; clean base for clean_base

historical_recipe.training_order: Separate completed installations. First adapter merges into a saved checkpoint; a fresh second adapter trains on that checkpoint. This differs from the historical same-run shuffled sequential files.

minimal_generation_adapter.image: Reuse completion_app.image and its locked dependencies. Supply no OpenRouter secret to GPU workers.
interface: base_path or pinned remote base id
minimal_generation_adapter.loader: For historical merged sources, load tokenizer and model from base_path with local_files_only=True; verify all source files before and after load; then attach the second-stage adapter with PeftModel.from_pretrained. Do not supply the clean-base revision check to a local merged config that lacks a commit hash.
minimal_generation_adapter.guard: Require run_config.base_model and adapter_config.base_model_name_or_path to match the declared historical base_path. Compare the expected hashes and reject missing or changed files. Never call _ensure_merged_checkpoint, _seq_cell_body, train_lora, or merge_adapter as a fallback.
minimal_generation_adapter.output: Persist every prompt, raw response, generation settings, model/base/adapter hashes, tokenizer/chat-template hashes, seeds, dependency versions, and completion handles under the new follow-up namespace.
minimal_generation_adapter.existing_runner_limitation: completion_generation.py hardcodes a clean Qwen base and its revision. It cannot load second-stage historical adapters correctly without an explicit merged-base extension.
minimal_generation_adapter.controls: Load individual controls as the bare saved merged models. Base+first-adapter can have small numerical differences from the saved bfloat16 merge; use the saved phase-one model for retention.

interpretation_limits: The first mover trained only on its distinct cue. At overlap 1, only the second mover received shared-cue positives. Shared-cue second-mover wins therefore do not establish a symmetric contest between two trained shared-cue loyalties.

The current hash inventory identifies recovered present files. Historical metadata does not pin the original clean-base commit, runtime environment, tensor hashes, or dataset hashes. It cannot prove immutable historical byte identity.

Complete finite tensors and matching paths establish structural readiness, not the historical causal chain. The original lazy merge routine had a documented concurrency race. Do not use it to recreate missing files.
The original symmetric judge collapses both-supported and neither-supported responses. Use independent canonical stance judgments and preserve raw responses in this follow-up.
A and B have different training row totals because source banks have minor row shortfalls. Exact current row totals are preserved in the dataset records.
Two historical training seeds limit replication. Prompt samples do not supply additional independent training seeds.
Historical CSVs preserve only aggregate judgments, so a new run cannot recover the old random responses.
